visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Rail's revenue rises from 400 to 500, and Bus's from 100 to 140. Which grew faster?
questions.explain: Fast means a percentage: Bus grew 40 on 100, or 40%, and Rail grew 100 on 400, or 25%. Rail's jump is bigger in euros, but slower.
questions.explain_at: You answered how much, and the question asked how fast

questions.q: Rail was 400 of a group's 800, and it's now 500 of 1,000. What happened to its share of revenue?

options.text: It rose by 25%, with its revenue
It fell as the group grew

questions.explain: 400 of 800 and 500 of 1,000 are both a half. Rail grew at the same pace as the group, so its share didn't move.
questions.explain_at: Its revenue grew at the same pace as the group

questions.q: What's $500m in euros, at 1.25 dollars to the euro?
questions.explain: One euro buys more than a dollar, so you end up with fewer euros than dollars: divide 500 by 1.25. Multiplying gives €625m, the wrong direction.
questions.explain_at: One euro buys more than a dollar, so you must end up with fewer euros

questions.q: You've used up your time on a test question and you're still stuck. What should you do?

options.text: Stay on it until you've solved it
Go back and recheck earlier answers
Pick your best estimate and move on
Work it out exactly before answering

questions.explain: Your time per question is a budget. Minutes spent stuck on one question come out of the ones that follow.
questions.explain_at: A hundred and eight seconds is a budget

questions.q: Eurocommercial sold 5.2m new shares at €24.70, a discount to the €26 close. Roughly how much did that raise?
questions.explain: The new investors paid €24.70, not the €26 close: 5.2m times €24.70 is about €128m. Using the close gives €135m.
questions.explain_at: Twenty-six is the close, and the new investors paid twenty-four seventy
